guidelines.detail: same as LRN-047 (The description gives customer-selected options and describes downstream work that depends on those specifications. The missing gateway and flows indicate that the choice and its routing were not represented; LRN-047 already states essentially the same modeling guidance.)

same as LRN-030 (The description says requirements go to different teams and assembly follows receipt of the individual components. This supports parallel production branches joined before assembly; LRN-030 already expresses essentially the same rule.)

The records show label differences, but several reference labels conflict with the description: it says to create the test protocol, send requirements to different teams (including Russian and Irish teams), and deliver the plane. The corresponding reference labels instead say to update the protocol, specify an American team, and send the plane. Those differences do not support a guideline to reproduce the reference labels. The remaining label differences are either compatible paraphrases or not clearly shown to be errors against the description.

same as LRN-056 (The description states customization choices and ordered handoffs; the missing-flow records show those relationships were not preserved. This is already covered in substance by learned guideline LRN-056, which calls for explicit modeling that preserves stated sequence, branches, and synchronization.)

same as LRN-046 (The label-pair records show that generated labels sometimes omit meaningful scope or recipients, or add or alter action details. The description supports preserving those distinctions in labels. This is essentially covered by learned guideline LRN-046, which calls for concise, faithful labels preserving applicable scope or criteria without unsupported meaning.)

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says that a person selects an option and that subsequent actions depend on which option was selected: Model the selection as an activity, then use a gateway to route the resulting alternatives.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that a person selects among alternatives and that later work depends on the selected option.

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states a meaningful object, recipient, or responsible role for an activity: Use a concise BPMN label that preserves the described action and those details when they distinguish or clarify the activity.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states an activity and specifies its action, scope, or distinguishing details

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says that independent activities proceed while other work is underway and that a later activity depends on all of them being complete: Model the concurrent activities with a parallel split, then synchronize all required branches with a parallel join before the dependent activity.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that separate work items are produced independently and that a later activity begins only after all required items have been received

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states distinct activities or decisions within a workflow, along with outcomes or dependencies between them: Model those activities and decisions as explicit elements at the process level needed to preserve the stated sequence, branches, and synchronization; do not collapse them into a generic subprocess that obscures that structure.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states an activity sequence, decision, or synchronization

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states an action or decision represented by a BPMN element, including any applicable scope or criteria: Label the element with concise wording that faithfully reflects the stated action or decision and preserves any applicable scope or criteria, without implying unsupported meaning or broader applicability.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states an activity's action together with meaningful scope, qualifiers, or recipients
